with ![images](images/c14-i0106.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>&#963;</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>&#963;</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">&#934;</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.

A straightforward implementation of the Yule-Walker and Durbin-Levinson algorithms is given by the functions `.quantQ.ts.YuleWalker[p;data]` and `.quantQ.ts.DurbinLevinson[data;p]` described in the second part of the chapter. The least square method produces the same estimates of the ![images](images/c14-i0107.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> parameters as solving the Yule-Walker equations but is much slower than the iterative approach. The Durbin-Levinson algorithm is twice as fast as inverting the Toeplitz matrix ![images](images/c14-i0108.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix">&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></math>.

![](images/c14-gra-0008.png)

returns:

![](images/c14-gra-0009.png)

However,

![](images/c14-gra-0010.png)

shows that it takes 913 milliseconds to estimate the parameters of ![images](images/c14-i0109.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>000</mn></mrow></math> random numbers following the ![images](images/c14-i0110.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> model ![images](images/c14-i0111.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.4</mn><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>0.3</mn><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math> by solving the OLS estimator while it takes 26 milliseconds by inverting the Toeplitz matrix and only 12 milliseconds by solving the Durbin-Levinson iterative algorithm:

![](images/c14-gra-0011.png) 

### 14.1.3 ![images](images/c14-i0112.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi>M</mi> <mi>A</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>q</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </math> Process

Autoregressive processes are long memory models. They generally have an infinite non-zero autocorrelation decaying over time. Autoregressive processes cannot represent short memory series, where the current value of the series ![images](images/c14-i0113.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math> is only correlated with a few past values ![images](images/c14-i0114.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>. This section presents moving average processes that are generally a function of a small number of past innovations.

A moving average process of order ![images](images/c14-i0115.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow></math>, denoted as ![images](images/c14-i0116.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, is defined as:

[(14.13)](#c14.xhtml#R_c14-disp-0020)![equation](images/c14-math-0020.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mi>X</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mi>c</mi> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>&#949;</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>&#945;</mi> <mn>1</mn> </msub> <msub> <mi>&#949;</mi> <mrow> <mi>t</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>&#945;</mi> <mn>2</mn> </msub> <msub> <mi>&#949;</mi> <mrow> <mi>t</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mn>2</mn> </mrow> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>&#945;</mi> <mi>q</mi> </msub> <msub> <mi>&#949;</mi> <mrow> <mi>t</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mi>q</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

where ![images](images/c14-i0117.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mi>q</mi></msub></mrow></math> are the parameters of the model, ![images](images/c14-i0118.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> a constant, and {![images](images/c14-i0119.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#949;</mi></mrow></math>} the white noise, i.e. ![images](images/c14-i0120.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>&#8764;</mo><mi>W</mi><mi mathvariant="double-struck">N</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>&#963;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. The ![images](images/c14-i0121.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process is stationary by construction. Its expectation is ![images](images/c14-i0122.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> and variance is ![images](images/c14-i0123.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>V</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>&#947;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>&#963;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>&#945;</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>&#945;</mi><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>+</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>&#945;</mi><mi>q</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.

The autocorrelation ![images](images/c14-i0124.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#947;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfenced open="{" close="" separators=""><mtable><mtr><mtd class="array"><msup><mi>&#963;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="1em"/></mtd><mtd class="array"><mi>s</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>q</mi></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="array"><mn>0</mn><mspace width="1em"/></mtd><mtd class="array"><mi>s</mi><mo>&#62;</mo><mi>q</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable></mfenced></mrow></math>. Suppose that ![images](images/c14-i0125.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math> is a zero-mean series with finite variance for each time ![images](images/c14-i0126.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c14-i0127.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>&#947;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, where the matrix ![images](images/c14-i0128.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>&#947;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup></mrow></math> is non-singular for each ![images](images/c14-i0129.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow></math>.

The one-step predictor of the ![images](images/c14-i0130.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process is given by:

![equation](images/c14-math-0021.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>X</mi><mo>&#94;</mo></mover><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfenced open="{" close="" separators=""><mtable><mtr><mtd class="array"><mn>0</mn><mspace width="1em"/></mtd><mtd class="array"><mspace width="0.3em"/><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="array"><msubsup><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#945;</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mrow><mi>n</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&#8722;</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>X</mi><mo>&#94;</mo></mover><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="1em"/></mtd><mtd class="array"><mspace width="0.3em"/><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8805;</mo><mn>1</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable></mfenced><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> 

The one-step predictors ![images](images/c14-i0131.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>X</mi><mo>&#94;</mo></mover><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>X</mi><mo>&#94;</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> can be computed recursively once the coefficients ![images](images/c14-i0132.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#945;</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> have been determined by the innovations algorithm [14.14](#c14.xhtml#c14-disp-0024).

 

#### *14.1.3.1 Estimation of ![images](images/c14-i0133.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> Parameters*

While the Durbin-Levinson algorithm gives the estimates of the coefficients in the representation:

![equation](images/c14-math-0022.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>X</mi><mo>&#94;</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><munderover><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>p</mi></munderover><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#945;</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo></mrow></math> 

where ![images](images/c14-i0134.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#945;</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c14-i0135.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> are the parameters of the model, the innovations algorithm used to estimate the parameters of the ![images](images/c14-i0136.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process [14.13](#c14.xhtml#c14-disp-0020) considers the representation:

![equation](images/c14-math-0023.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>X</mi><mo>&#94;</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><munderover><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></munderover><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#952;</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&#8722;</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>X</mi><mo>&#94;</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> 

As for the ![images](images/c14-i0137.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process, let us rewrite the ![images](images/c14-i0138.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process with a double suffix ![images](images/c14-i0139.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>. Starting with ![images](images/c14-i0140.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>&#963;</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mn>0</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#947;</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, the estimator of ![images](images/c14-i0141.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#945;</mi></mrow></math> recursively solves:

[(14.14)](#c14.xhtml#R_c14-disp-0024)![equation](images/c14-math-0024.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mover accent="true"> <mi>&#945;</mi> <mo>&#770;</mo> </mover> <mrow> <mi>q</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>q</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mi>k</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mfrac> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi>&#947;</mi> <mo>&#770;</mo> </mover> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>q</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mi>k</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <msubsup> <mo movablelimits="false">&#8721;</mo> <mrow> <mi>j</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> </mrow> <mrow> <mi>k</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </msubsup> <msub> <mover accent="true"> <mi>&#945;</mi> <mo>&#770;</mo> </mover> <mrow> <mi>q</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>q</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mi>j</mi> </mrow> </msub> <msub> <mover accent="true"> <mi>&#945;</mi> <mo>&#770;</mo> </mover> <mrow> <mi>k</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>k</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mi>j</mi> </mrow> </msub> <msubsup> <mover accent="true"> <mi>&#963;</mi> <mo>&#770;</mo> </mover> <mi>j</mi> <mn>2</mn> </msubsup> </mrow> <msubsup> <mover accent="true"> <mi>&#963;</mi> <mo>&#770;</mo> </mover> <mi>k</mi> <mn>2</mn> </msubsup> </mfrac> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

for ![images](images/c14-i0142.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c14-i0143.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c14-i0144.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>&#963;</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mi>q</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>&#947;</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><msubsup><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>&#945;</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>&#963;</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mi>j</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></math>.

The innovations algorithm to estimate the parameters of the ![images](images/c14-i0145.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> model is implemented with the function `.quantQ.ts.innovations[data;q]`.

 

#### *14.1.3.2 Simulation*

A moving average process of order 1 is simulated as:

![equation](images/c14-math-0025.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mtable columnalign="left center right"><mtr><mtd class="eqnarray-1"><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mtd><mtd class="eqnarray-2"><mo>=</mo></mtd><mtd class="eqnarray-3"><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="eqnarray-1"><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mtd><mtd class="eqnarray-2"><mo>=</mo></mtd><mtd class="eqnarray-3"><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="eqnarray-1"/><mtd class="eqnarray-2"><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo></mtd><mtd/></mtr><mtr><mtd class="eqnarray-1"><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mtd><mtd class="eqnarray-2"><mo>=</mo></mtd><mtd class="eqnarray-3"><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>.</mo></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></math> 

Given a set of 5 random numbers ![images](images/c14-i0146.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></mrow></math>:

![](images/c14-gra-0012.png)

An![images](images/c14-i0147.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process is modelled as:

![](images/c14-gra-0013.png)

For ![images](images/c14-i0148.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#945;</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow></math>, the function returns:

![](images/c14-gra-0014.png)

Generic ![images](images/c14-i0149.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> models can be simulated with the recursive function `.quantQ.ts.simMA[q;alpha;eps]`.

![equation](images/c14-math-0026.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>0.5</mn><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>0.3</mn><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo></mrow></math>

### 14.1.4 ![images](images/c14-i0153.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi>A</mi> <mi>R</mi> <mi>M</mi> <mi>A</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>p</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>q</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </math> Process

The long memory ![images](images/c14-i0154.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> model can be combined with the short memory ![images](images/c14-i0155.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process to produce a new family of tractable and flexible stationary processes called ![images](images/c14-i0156.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. The autoregressive moving average process ![images](images/c14-i0157.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> refers to the model with ![images](images/c14-i0158.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> autoregressive terms and ![images](images/c14-i0159.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> moving average terms:

[(14.15)](#c14.xhtml#R_c14-disp-0027)![equation](images/c14-math-0027.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mi>X</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mi>c</mi> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>&#949;</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <munderover> <mo>&#8721;</mo> <mrow> <mi>i</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> <mi>p</mi> </munderover> <msub> <mi mathvariant="normal">&#934;</mi> <mi>i</mi> </msub> <msub> <mi>X</mi> <mrow> <mi>t</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mi>i</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <munderover> <mo>&#8721;</mo> <mrow> <mi>i</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> <mi>q</mi> </munderover> <msub> <mi>&#945;</mi> <mi>i</mi> </msub> <msub> <mi>&#949;</mi> <mrow> <mi>t</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mi>i</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

written with the lag operator ![images](images/c14-i0160.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>L</mi></mrow></math>, the ![images](images/c14-i0161.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process is:

![equation](images/c14-math-0028.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><munderover><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>p</mi></munderover><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">&#934;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><msup><mi>L</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><munderover><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>q</mi></munderover><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><msup><mi>L</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo></mrow></math> 

or more concisely

(14.16)![equation](images/c14-math-0029.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="normal">&#934;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>L</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <msub> <mi>X</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mi>c</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mi>&#945;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>L</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <msub> <mi>&#949;</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> <mo>.</mo> </mrow> </math>  

#### *14.1.4.1 Invertibility of the ![images](images/c14-i0162.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> Process*

Denoting ![images](images/c14-i0163.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#960;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#8801;</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">&#934;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>&#945;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> and provided that ![images](images/c14-i0164.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mi>&#8734;</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>&#960;</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>&#60;</mo><mi>&#8734;</mi></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c14-i0165.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#960;</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>, the ![images](images/c14-i0166.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process can be presented as an ![images](images/c14-i0167.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>&#8734;</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> model presented in [14.1](#c14.xhtml#c14-disp-0001):

![equation](images/c14-math-0030.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mtable columnalign="left center right"><mtr><mtd class="eqnarray-1"><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mtd><mtd class="eqnarray-2"><mo>=</mo></mtd><mtd class="eqnarray-3"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>&#945;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">&#934;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="eqnarray-1"/><mtd class="eqnarray-2"><mo>=</mo></mtd><mtd class="eqnarray-3"><mi>&#960;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>c</mi></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="eqnarray-1"/><mtd class="eqnarray-2"><mo>=</mo></mtd><mtd class="eqnarray-3"><munderover><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mi>&#8734;</mi></munderover><msub><mi>&#960;</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><msup><mi>L</mi><mi>j</mi></msup><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>c</mi></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="eqnarray-1"/><mtd class="eqnarray-2"><mo>=</mo></mtd><mtd class="eqnarray-3"><munderover><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mi>&#8734;</mi></munderover><msub><mi>&#960;</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>.</mo></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></math>  

#### *14.1.4.2 Hannan-Rissanen Algorithm: Two-Step Regression Estimation*

![images](images/c14-i0168.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi>A</mi> <mi>R</mi> <mi>M</mi> <mi>A</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>p</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>q</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </math> processes are a combination of autoregressive ![images](images/c14-i0169.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and moving average ![images](images/c14-i0170.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> processes. The ![images](images/c14-i0171.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> parameters ![images](images/c14-i0172.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold">&#934;</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">&#934;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">&#934;</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c14-i0173.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#945;</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c14-i0174.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi>&#963;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math> can be estimated with a two-step regression:

*   Step 1: Regress ![images](images/c14-i0175.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math> on its past values ![images](images/c14-i0176.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c14-i0177.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>&#62;</mo><mi>max</mi><mo stretchy="false">&#123;</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">&#125;</mo></mrow></math>, and derive the OLS estimates of ![images](images/c14-i0178.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#960;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c14-i0179.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></math> and the estimation of the residuals ![images](images/c14-i0180.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#949;</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>&#8722;</mo><msubsup><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#960;</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>.
*   Step 2: Regress ![images](images/c14-i0181.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math> on ![images](images/c14-i0182.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c14-i0183.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#949;</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#949;</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>.

#### *14.1.4.4 Maximum Likelihood Estimation*

Let![images](images/c14-i0188.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#952;</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">&#934;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">&#934;</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>&#963;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mrow></math> denote the parameters of the ![images](images/c14-i0189.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process and let ![images](images/c14-i0190.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mtext mathvariant="bold">x</mtext><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mi>x</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mrow></math> be the observed sample of size ![images](images/c14-i0191.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow></math>. The joint probability density function of the data given the parameter ![images](images/c14-i0192.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#952;</mi></mrow></math> is ![images](images/c14-i0193.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mi>x</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>&#952;</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. The likelihood function of the parameter ![images](images/c14-i0194.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#952;</mi></mrow></math> given ![images](images/c14-i0195.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mtext mathvariant="bold">x</mtext></mrow></math> is ![images](images/c14-i0196.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>&#952;</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mtext mathvariant="bold">x</mtext><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mi>x</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>&#952;</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. The maximum likelihood estimation is:

![equation](images/c14-math-0032.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mover accent="true"><mi>&#952;</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mrow><mi>M</mi><mi>L</mi><mi>E</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mtext mathvariant="normal">arg</mtext><mspace width="0.15em"/><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>&#952;</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">&#920;</mi></mrow></munder><mspace width="0.15em"/><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>&#952;</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mtext mathvariant="bold">x</mtext><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mtext mathvariant="normal">arg</mtext><mspace width="0.15em"/><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>&#952;</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">&#920;</mi></mrow></munder><mi mathvariant="normal">log</mi><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>&#952;</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mtext mathvariant="bold">x</mtext><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> 

Assuming that the error of the ![images](images/c14-i0199.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process is Gaussian, ![images](images/c14-i0200.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math>![images](images/c14-i0201.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo>&#8764;</mo><mi>W</mi><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>&#963;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, the likelihood is:

![equation](images/c14-math-0033.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>&#952;</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mtext mathvariant="bold">x</mtext><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>&#960;</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo form="prefix">&#8722;</mo><mi>T</mi><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">&#915;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>&#952;</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix">&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">exp</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix">&#8722;</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mtext mathvariant="bold">x</mtext><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">&#915;</mi><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>&#952;</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo form="prefix">&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mtext mathvariant="bold">x</mtext><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo></mrow></math> 

where the ![images](images/c14-i0202.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></math> variance-covariance matrix of x is ![images](images/c14-i0203.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">&#915;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>&#952;</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mtext mathvariant="bold">x</mtext><msup><mtext mathvariant="bold">x</mtext><mo mathvariant="bold">&#8242;</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>. The log-likelihood to optimise is:

(14.17)![equation](images/c14-math-0034.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi>l</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>&#952;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">|</mo> <mtext mathvariant="bold">x</mtext> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>=</mo> <mi mathvariant="normal">log</mi> <mi>L</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>&#952;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">|</mo> <mtext mathvariant="bold">x</mtext> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>=</mo> <mo form="prefix">&#8722;</mo> <mfrac> <mn>1</mn> <mn>2</mn> </mfrac> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>T</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi mathvariant="normal">log</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mi>&#960;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>+</mo> <mi mathvariant="normal">log</mi> <mo stretchy="false">|</mo> <mi mathvariant="normal">&#915;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>&#952;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo stretchy="false">|</mo> <mo>+</mo> <msup> <mtext mathvariant="bold">x</mtext> <mo mathvariant="bold">&#8242;</mo> </msup> <mi mathvariant="normal">&#915;</mi> <msup> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>&#952;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mrow> <mo form="prefix">&#8722;</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </msup> <mtext mathvariant="bold">x</mtext> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>.</mo> </mrow> </math>

#### *14.1.4.6 Forecast*

The innovations algorithm [14.14](#c14.xhtml#c14-disp-0024) used to estimate and forecast the ![images](images/c14-i0206.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process can be adapted to forecast the ![images](images/c14-i0207.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> model. The one-step predictor is given by:

### 14.1.5 ![images](images/c14-i0209.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi>A</mi> <mi>R</mi> <mi>I</mi> <mi>M</mi> <mi>A</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>p</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>d</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>q</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </math> Process

The autoregressive integrated moving average process is a generalisation of the ![images](images/c14-i0210.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process. It is defined with three parameters: as for the ARMA process, ![images](images/c14-i0211.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> is the order of the autoregressive component and ![images](images/c14-i0212.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> is the order of the moving average of the process. The parameter ![images](images/c14-i0213.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>d</mi></mrow></math> indicates the order of the integration of the series. Let us define the lag-d difference operator ![images](images/c14-i0214.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mo>&#8711;</mo><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow></math> by ![images](images/c14-i0215.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mo>&#8711;</mo><mi>d</mi></msub><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>&#8722;</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><msup><mi>L</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math>. The process {![images](images/c14-i0216.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">Z</mi></mrow></math>} is said to be an ARIMA(p,d,q) process if ![images](images/c14-i0217.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mo>&#8711;</mo><mi>d</mi></msub><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math> is a causal ![images](images/c14-i0218.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process. A causal ![images](images/c14-i0219.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>I</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process {![images](images/c14-i0220.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math>} satisfies:

![equation](images/c14-math-0038.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">&#934;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">&#934;</mi><mo>&#42;</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi></msup><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>&#945;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo></mrow></math> 

with {![images](images/c14-i0221.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math>} ![images](images/c14-i0222.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo>&#8764;</mo><mi>W</mi><mi mathvariant="double-struck">N</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>&#963;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> where ![images](images/c14-i0223.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">&#934;</mi><mo>&#42;</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#8800;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>![images](images/c14-i0224.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#8704;</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo>&#8804;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>. The process ![images](images/c14-i0225.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mo>&#8711;</mo><mi>d</mi></msub><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>I</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi></msup><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math> satisfies

(14.18)![equation](images/c14-math-0039.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msup> <mi mathvariant="normal">&#934;</mi> <mo>&#42;</mo> </msup> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>L</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <msub> <mi>Y</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mi>&#945;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>L</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <msub> <mi>&#949;</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> <mo>.</mo> </mrow> </math>  

### 14.1.6 Code

This section presents a `q` implementation of the algorithms presented in the chapter to simulate, estimate and forecast ![images](images/c14-i0226.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c14-i0227.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, and ![images](images/c14-i0228.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> processes. Three generic functions are used to simulate, estimate and forecast all models:

*   `.quantQ.ts.simulate[process;params;eps]`
*   `.quantQ.ts.estimate[data;process;lags]`
*   `.quantQ.ts.forecast[data;period;process;lags]`.

 

#### *14.1.6.1 Simulation*

The generic function `.quantQ.ts.simulate` simulates autoregressive, moving average and ARMA processes covered in the chapter. The function takes three arguments. The first argument `process` takes the value `‘AR`, `‘MA` and `‘ARMA`. The second parameter `params` contains the parameters of the model as a list of floating numbers. For ARMA models, `params` is of the form ((AR params; MA params)), where each sublist contains floating numbers.

![](images/c14-gra-0017.png)

The simulation of ![images](images/c14-i0229.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> model is performed by the function `.quant.ts.simAR`. The function simulates [14.1](#c14.xhtml#c14-disp-0001) given the list of parameters ![images](images/c14-i0230.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">&#934;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c14-i0231.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> and white noise ![images](images/c14-i0232.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#949;</mi></mrow></math>.

![](images/c14-gra-0018.png)

The simulation of moving average process [14.13](#c14.xhtml#c14-disp-0020) is computed recursively as follows:

![](images/c14-gra-0019.png)

The ![images](images/c14-i0233.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process [14.15](#c14.xhtml#c14-disp-0027) is simulated given the white noise process ![images](images/c14-i0234.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#949;</mi></mrow></math> and list of parameters for autoregressive coefficients ![images](images/c14-i0235.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">&#934;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c14-i0236.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> and moving average ![images](images/c14-i0237.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c14-i0238.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>:

![](images/c14-gra-0020.png) 

#### *14.1.6.2 Estimation*

The generic function `.quantQ.ts.estimate` estimates the coefficients of the autoregressive, moving average and ARMA processes. The function estimates the coefficients on the list of floating point numbers provided in the first argument. The second parameter `process` takes the value `‘AR`, `‘MA` or `‘ARMA` depending on the type of process to be estimated. The third parameter contains either an integer corresponding to the order of the autoregressive or moving average process or a list of two integers for the two lags of the ![images](images/c14-i0239.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process.

![](images/c14-gra-0021.png)

The autoregressive process ![images](images/c14-i0240.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is estimated with the Durbin-Levinson algorithm by default as the procedure is quicker than solving the Yule-Walker equation or inverting the matrix [14.6](#c14.xhtml#c14-disp-0008) to compute the OLS estimator. The Durbin-Levinson algorithm is implemented as follows:

![](images/c14-gra-0022.png)

Given the function `.quantQ.ts.toeplitz` to build the Toeplitz matrix [14.12](#c14.xhtml#c14-disp-0017) of sample autocorrelation `.quantQ.ts.r`, first, we define the sample autocovariance function of order `h`:

![](images/c14-gra-0023.png)

then the sample autocorrelation function of order `h`:

![](images/c14-gra-0024.png)

and, finally, the Toeplitz matrix:

![](images/c14-gra-0025.png)

The Yule-Walker equations can be solved as follows:

![](images/c14-gra-0026.png)

Finally, the OLS estimator [14.6](#c14.xhtml#c14-disp-0008) can be implemented as:

![](images/c14-gra-0027.png)

An implementation of the innovations algorithm [14.14](#c14.xhtml#c14-disp-0024) to estimate the coefficients of the ![images](images/c14-i0241.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process is provided as:

![](images/c14-gra-0028.png)

The innovations algorithm converges more slowly than the number of lags of the moving average process. Thus, we multiply the number of lags ![images](images/c14-i0242.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> by 10 to improve the estimator and select the ![images](images/c14-i0243.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> first element of the alpha matrix.

The parameters of the ![images](images/c14-i0244.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> are estimated by solving the Hannan-Rissanen algorithm with a two-step regression:

![](images/c14-gra-0029.png)

where the recursive helper function `.quantQ.ts.matrix` stacks the series ![images](images/c14-i0245.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>d</mi></mrow></math> into a matrix and computes `(d[t-q];d[t-q-1];...;d[t-1])`:

![](images/c14-gra-0030.png)

The implementation of the estimator for the ![images](images/c14-i0246.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>I</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process is left as an exercise for our readers. It can be estimated by modifying the Yule-Walker equation of the ![images](images/c14-i0247.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process or by adapting the Hannan-Rissanen algorithm.

 

#### *14.1.6.3 Forecast*

The generic function `.quantQ.ts.forecast[data;period;process;lags]` forecasts `period`-step ahead the `process` of order `lags` based on the data set `data`. The parameter `data` is a list of floating numbers. The argument `period` is a positive integer. The variable `process` contains the values `‘AR` for autoregressive process, `‘MA` for moving average process or `‘ARMA` for autoregressive moving average processes. The fourth parameter `lags` is positive integer or list of two positive integers for ![images](images/c14-i0248.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> models.

![](images/c14-gra-0031.png)

The autoregressive forecasting subroutine is implemented recursively as:

![](images/c14-gra-0032.png)

To forecast a ![images](images/c14-i0249.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process, we assume that the estimated model is the true model and fill in unknown values with predictions. Let's take an ![images](images/c14-i0250.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process as an example:

![equation](images/c14-math-0040.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> 

The one-step forecast is:

![equation](images/c14-math-0041.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mtable columnalign="left center right"><mtr><mtd class="eqnarray-1"><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mtd><mtd class="eqnarray-2"><mo>=</mo></mtd><mtd class="eqnarray-3"><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="eqnarray-1"><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>X</mi><mo>&#94;</mo></mover><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mtd><mtd class="eqnarray-2"><mo>=</mo></mtd><mtd class="eqnarray-3"><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#945;</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></math> 

with ![images](images/c14-i0251.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>&#8722;</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>X</mi><mo>&#94;</mo></mover><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></math> and variance ![images](images/c14-i0252.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>V</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>&#8722;</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>X</mi><mo>&#94;</mo></mover><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>&#963;</mi></mrow></math>. The two-step forecast solves:
