If the function `.quantQ.ts.forecastARMA` will not be implemented, the function `.quantQ.ts.forecast` has to be simply amended to tackle the case of `ARMA`.

 

## 14.2 STATIONARITY AND GRANGER CAUSALITY

 

### 14.2.1 Stationarity

A stochastic process is said to be stationary if its statistical properties do not change with time. Formally, a time series ![images](images/c14-i0263.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c14-i0264.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">Z</mi></mrow></math> is weakly stationary or wide sense stationary if:

*   It has a finite variance: ![images](images/c14-i0265.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>V</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#60;</mo><mi>&#8734;</mi></mrow></math>![images](images/c14-i0266.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#8704;</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">Z</mi></mrow></math>.
*   The mean is constant: ![images](images/c14-i0267.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mi>&#956;</mi><mi>X</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>&#956;</mi></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c14-i0268.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#8704;</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">Z</mi></mrow></math>.
*   The autocovariance does not depend on time ![images](images/c14-i0269.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c14-i0270.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#8704;</mi><mi>r</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">Z</mi></mrow></math>.

A process is said to be strictly stationary if any finite collection ![images](images/c14-i0271.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> has the same distribution as ![images](images/c14-i0272.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> for any ![images](images/c14-i0273.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>&#8805;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c14-i0274.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#8712;</mo><mi mathvariant="double-struck">Z</mi></mrow></math>.

 

### 14.2.2 Test of Stationarity – Dickey-Fuller and Augmented Dickey-Fuller Tests

The Dickey-Fuller (DF) test tests the null hypothesis that a unit root is present in an autoregressive model. The test estimates three models:

*   The first model is an ![images](images/c14-i0275.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process without constant: ![images](images/c14-i0276.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>&#961;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math>.
*   The second model is an ![images](images/c14-i0277.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process with constant: ![images](images/c14-i0278.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>&#946;</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#961;</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math>.
*   The third model adds a trend to the ![images](images/c14-i0279.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> with constant: ![images](images/c14-i0280.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>&#956;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#946;</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#961;</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math>.

The first model can be rewritten as ![images](images/c14-i0281.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">&#916;</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>&#961;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>&#966;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math>, the second model ![images](images/c14-i0282.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">&#916;</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>&#956;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#966;</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math> and the third ![images](images/c14-i0283.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">&#916;</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>&#956;</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>&#946;</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#966;</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math>.

The DF test tests the stationarity of ![images](images/c14-i0284.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> processes. The test can be augmented to detect unit root for ![images](images/c14-i0285.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. It is called Augmented Dickey–Fuller (ADF) test. The ADF test estimates three models:

*   The ![images](images/c14-i0286.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> model without constant: ![images](images/c14-i0287.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">&#916;</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>&#966;</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mi>p</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>&#946;</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">&#916;</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math>.
*   The ![images](images/c14-i0288.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> model with constant: ![images](images/c14-i0289.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">&#916;</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>&#956;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>&#966;</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mi>p</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>&#946;</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">&#916;</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math>.
*   The ![images](images/c14-i0290.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> model with constant and trend: ![images](images/c14-i0291.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">&#916;</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>&#956;</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>&#946;</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>&#966;</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mi>p</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>&#946;</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">&#916;</mi><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>&#949;</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math>.

The null hypothesis of the ADF test is the non-stationarity (unit root) of the variable ![images](images/c14-i0292.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math>, i.e. ![images](images/c14-i0293.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>:</mo><mi>&#966;</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>. The ADF test compares the Student-t associated with the parameter ![images](images/c14-i0294.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#966;</mi></mrow></math> with the tabulated values of the statistics given by MacKinnon (1996). The null hypothesis of non-stationarity is rejected at 5% if ![images](images/c14-i0295.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mi>b</mi><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&#60;</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>D</mi><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>0.05</mn></msub></mrow></math>. The optimal number of lags of ![images](images/c14-i0296.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> can be determined with the AIC test described in [Chapter 13](#c13.xhtml) dedicated to linear regression and implemented with the function `.quantQ.ols.AIC:[p;logL]`.

To determine whether to retain the hypothesis of a unit root with or without a constant, the Student-![images](images/c14-i0297.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> associated with the constant ![images](images/c14-i0298.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#956;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> is compared with the tabulated values of the statistics. For the third model, the ADF test checks whether the estimated values of the coefficients associated with the constant (![images](images/c14-i0299.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#956;</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math>) and trend (![images](images/c14-i0300.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#946;</mi></mrow></math>) are significantly different from zero with ![images](images/c14-i0301.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>:</mo><msub><mi>&#956;</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c14-i0302.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>:</mo><msub><mi>&#946;</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></math>.

The ![images](images/c14-i0303.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">&#916;</mi></mrow></math> of a time series `data` is simply `deltas data`. The three autoregressive models can be estimated with the function `.quantQ.ts.DurbinLevinson[data;q]`. Tabulated values of the statistics given by MacKinnon can be stored in a dictionary and compared with the t-stat ![images](images/c14-i0304.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mi>b</mi><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> as implemented in the function `.quantQ.ols.fit`.

 

### 14.2.3 Granger Causality

The models presented so far are, somehow, limited. They only use past realisations of a random variable to explain its current and future values. In addition to the use of past values of a random variable to forecast its future, a model can often be improved by adding historical values of external factors, also called exogenous variables. An autoregressive process of order p with exogenous variables, denoted as ![images](images/c14-i0305.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, is given by:

(14.19)![equation](images/c14-math-0045.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mi>Y</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mi>a</mi> <mn>0</mn> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>a</mi> <mn>1</mn> </msub> <msub> <mi>Y</mi> <mrow> <mi>t</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>a</mi> <mi>p</mi> </msub> <msub> <mi>Y</mi> <mrow> <mi>t</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mi>p</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>b</mi> <mn>1</mn> </msub> <msub> <mi>X</mi> <mrow> <mi>t</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>b</mi> <mi>p</mi> </msub> <msub> <mi>X</mi> <mrow> <mi>t</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mi>p</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>&#949;</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> <mo>.</mo> </mrow> </math> 

By the same token, an ![images](images/c14-i0306.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process is defined as:

(14.20)![equation](images/c14-math-0046.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mi>Y</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mi>a</mi> <mn>0</mn> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>&#949;</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <munderover> <mo>&#8721;</mo> <mrow> <mi>i</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> <mi>p</mi> </munderover> <msub> <mi>a</mi> <mi>i</mi> </msub> <msub> <mi>Y</mi> <mrow> <mi>t</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mi>i</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <munderover> <mo>&#8721;</mo> <mrow> <mi>i</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> <mi>p</mi> </munderover> <msub> <mi>b</mi> <mi>i</mi> </msub> <msub> <mi>X</mi> <mrow> <mi>t</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mi>i</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <munderover> <mo>&#8721;</mo> <mrow> <mi>i</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> <mi>q</mi> </munderover> <msub> <mi>c</mi> <mi>i</mi> </msub> <msub> <mi>&#949;</mi> <mrow> <mi>t</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mi>i</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>.</mo> </mrow> </math> 

The parameters of these two models with exogenous variables can be estimated with the same methods as their based models. To determine whether the lagged values of an exogenous variable explain the current and future values of a random variable, we introduce the Granger Causality test. The Granger Causality test is a statistical hypothesis test for determining whether an external time series ![images](images/c14-i0307.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is useful in forecasting another, say ![images](images/c14-i0308.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. A time series ![images](images/c14-i0309.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>X</mi></mrow></math> is said to Granger-cause![images](images/c14-i0310.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>Y</mi></mrow></math> if it can be shown, by running a ![images](images/c14-i0311.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math>\-test or an ![images](images/c14-i0312.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>F</mi></mrow></math>\-test on lagged values of ![images](images/c14-i0313.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>X</mi></mrow></math>, that those historical values of ![images](images/c14-i0314.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>X</mi></mrow></math> provide statistically significant information about future values of ![images](images/c14-i0315.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>Y</mi></mrow></math>. To find out whether ![images](images/c14-i0316.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>X</mi></mrow></math> Granger-uses ![images](images/c14-i0317.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>Y</mi></mrow></math>, we compare the ![images](images/c14-i0318.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> model with the corresponding ![images](images/c14-i0319.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> model and perform a ![images](images/c14-i0320.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math>\-test for individual coefficients with the null hypothesis ![images](images/c14-i0321.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>:</mo></mrow></math>![images](images/c14-i0322.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> against the alternative hypothesis ![images](images/c14-i0323.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> that at least one coefficient is non-zero.

We can also run an F-test:

![equation](images/c14-math-0047.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mi>u</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>l</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>&#8722;</mo><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>l</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><mi>n</mi><mi>b</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>V</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mi>u</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>l</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mi>b</mi><mi>O</mi><mi>b</mi><mi>s</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>n</mi><mi>b</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>F</mi><mi>u</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>l</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>,</mo></mrow></math> 

and compare it with ![images](images/c14-i0324.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi>F</mi><mo>&#42;</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mi>b</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mi>b</mi><mi>O</mi><mi>b</mi><mi>s</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>n</mi><mi>b</mi><mi>P</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>F</mi><mi>u</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>M</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. The null hypothesis of no Granger causality is rejected if ![images](images/c14-i0325.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>&#62;</mo><msup><mi>F</mi><mo>&#42;</mo></msup></mrow></math>. Note that the Granger Causality test suffers from some limitations such as:

*   Granger Causality is not necessarily true causality.
*   The Granger Causality often fails if an exogenous variable X affects Y through another time series Z.
*   When X(t) is autocorrelated, the impact of lagged values of X on Y(t) is simply a consequence of the impact of X(t) on Y(t).

A `q` implementation of the ![images](images/c14-i0326.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>F</mi></mrow></math>\-test presented in the previous chapter is `.quantQ.ols.fStatistics`.

 

## 14.3 VECTOR AUTOREGRESSION

This chapter generalises the univariate autoregressive and moving average process to capture the linear interdependencies among multiple time series. Simply speaking a vector autoregressive model ![images](images/c14-i0327.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>V</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> is a generalisation of an ![images](images/c14-i0328.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process where the random variable ![images](images/c14-i0329.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math> is replaced with a vector of random variables ![images](images/c14-i0330.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mi>X</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.

 

### 14.3.1 ![images](images/c14-i0331.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi>V</mi> <mi>A</mi> <mi>R</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>p</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </math> Process

The vector autoregressive process (VAR) of order ![images](images/c14-i0332.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> is given by

[(14.21)](#c14.xhtml#R_c14-disp-0048)![equation](images/c14-math-0048.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mi>Y</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mi>&#957;</mi> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>A</mi> <mn>1</mn> </msub> <msub> <mi>Y</mi> <mrow> <mi>t</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>A</mi> <mi>p</mi> </msub> <msub> <mi>Y</mi> <mrow> <mi>t</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mi>p</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>u</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

for ![images](images/c14-i0333.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> where ![images](images/c14-i0334.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mi>u</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mrow></math> is a K-dimensional white noise or innovation process with ![images](images/c14-i0335.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c14-i0336.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><msubsup><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mo>&#931;</mo><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c14-i0337.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><msubsup><mi>u</mi><mi>s</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> for ![images](images/c14-i0338.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>&#8800;</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></math>.

 

#### *14.3.1.1 Notation*

Let us assume that ![images](images/c14-i0339.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mi>y</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></math> is available for each of the ![images](images/c14-i0340.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>K</mi></mrow></math> variables for the same sample period. We introduce the following notations:

*   ![images](images/c14-i0341.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mi>y</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mrow></math> a ![images](images/c14-i0342.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></math> matrix
*   ![images](images/c14-i0343.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>&#957;</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> a ![images](images/c14-i0344.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>K</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> matrix
*   ![images](images/c14-i0345.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""><mtable><mtr><mtd columnalign="center"><mn>1</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center"><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center"><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center"><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mtd></mtr></mtable></mfenced></mrow></math> a ![images](images/c14-i0346.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>K</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#215;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> matrix
*   ![images](images/c14-i0347.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mi>Z</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> a ![images](images/c14-i0348.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>K</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></math> matrix
*   ![images](images/c14-i0349.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mi>u</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> a ![images](images/c14-i0350.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></math> matrix
*   ![images](images/c14-i0351.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>v</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> a ![images](images/c14-i0352.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>K</mi><mi>T</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> matrix
*   ![images](images/c14-i0353.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#946;</mi><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>v</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> a ![images](images/c14-i0354.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>K</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#215;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> matrix
*   ![images](images/c14-i0355.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>v</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> a ![images](images/c14-i0356.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>K</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>K</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#215;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> matrix
*   ![images](images/c14-i0357.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>v</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>U</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> a ![images](images/c14-i0358.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>K</mi><mi>T</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> matrix.

 

#### *14.3.1.2 Estimator*

An unbiased estimator of a ![images](images/c14-i0359.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>V</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process defined in [14.21](#c14.xhtml#c14-disp-0048) is

[(14.22)](#c14.xhtml#R_c14-disp-0049)![equation](images/c14-math-0049.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mi>B</mi> <mo>&#94;</mo> </mover> <mo>=</mo> <mi>Y</mi> <msup> <mi>Z</mi> <mo>&#8242;</mo> </msup> <msup> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>Z</mi> <msup> <mi>Z</mi> <mo>&#8242;</mo> </msup> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mrow> <mo form="prefix">&#8722;</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </msup> <mo>.</mo> </mrow> </math> 

The estimator of the variance-covariance matrix of the residual is given by:

[(14.23)](#c14.xhtml#R_c14-disp-0050)![equation](images/c14-math-0050.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"> <mover accent="true"> <mo>&#931;</mo> <mo>&#770;</mo> </mover> <mi>U</mi> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mfrac> <mn>1</mn> <mrow> <mi>T</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mi>K</mi> <mi>p</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </mfrac> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>Y</mi> <msup> <mi>Y</mi> <mo>&#8242;</mo> </msup> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mi>Y</mi> <msup> <mi>Z</mi> <mo>&#8242;</mo> </msup> <msup> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>Z</mi> <msup> <mi>Z</mi> <mo>&#8242;</mo> </msup> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mrow> <mo form="prefix">&#8722;</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </msup> <mi>Z</mi> <msup> <mi>Y</mi> <mo>&#8242;</mo> </msup> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>.</mo> </mrow> </math> 

To estimate whether the estimated coefficients ![images](images/c14-i0360.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>B</mi><mo>&#94;</mo></mover></mrow></math> of the model are significant, we can compare the associated element of ![images](images/c14-i0361.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math>\-ratios matrix

[(14.24)](#c14.xhtml#R_c14-disp-0051)![equation](images/c14-math-0051.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mfrac> <mover accent="true"> <mi>B</mi> <mo>&#94;</mo> </mover> <msqrt> <mrow> <mi>d</mi> <mi>i</mi> <mi>a</mi> <mi>g</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <msub> <mover accent="true"> <mo>&#931;</mo> <mo>&#770;</mo> </mover> <mi>u</mi> </msub> <mo>&#8855;</mo> <msup> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>Z</mi> <msup> <mi>Z</mi> <mo>&#8242;</mo> </msup> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mrow> <mo form="prefix">&#8722;</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </msup> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msqrt> </mfrac> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

with the critical values from a ![images](images/c14-i0362.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math>\-distribution with ![images](images/c14-i0363.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>K</mi><mi>T</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><msup><mi>K</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></math> degrees of freedom. The operator ![images](images/c14-i0364.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo>&#8855;</mo></mrow></math> is the Kronecker product and diag is the diagonal of the matrix ![images](images/c14-i0365.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mo>&#931;</mo><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>&#8855;</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><msup><mi>Z</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo form="prefix">&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>. Assuming that ![images](images/c14-i0366.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math> is Gaussian, an approximation of a ![images](images/c14-i0367.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>&#945;</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> interval forecast h-step ahead for k-th component ![images](images/c14-i0368.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is ![images](images/c14-i0369.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><msub><mi>&#375;</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#177;</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>&#945;</mi><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><msub><mover accent="true"><mover accent="true"><mi>&#963;</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>. stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is the ![images](images/c14-i0373.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mrow><mo distribution.

with ![images](images/c14-i0374.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">&#915;</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><msub><mi>Z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><msubsup><mi>Z</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c14-i0375.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>&#966;</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>J</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msup><mover accent="true"><mtext mathvariant="bold">B</mtext><mo mathvariant="bold">&#770;</mo></mover><mtext mathvariant="bold">i</mtext></msup><msubsup><mi>J</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8242;</mo></msubsup></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c14-i0376.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mn>0</mn><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>:</mo><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mi>I</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo>:</mo><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mn>0</mn><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>:</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>:</mo><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mn>0</mn><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> a ![images](images/c14-i0377.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>K</mi><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> matrix.

The order of a ![images](images/c14-i0378.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>V</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process is usually unknown and needs to be determined. Choosing an unnecessarily large value of ![images](images/c14-i0379.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> reduces the forecast precision the model. ![images](images/c14-i0380.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math> is called a ![images](images/c14-i0381.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>V</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process if ![images](images/c14-i0382.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>&#8800;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c14-i0383.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> for ![images](images/c14-i0384.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&#62;</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> so that the ![images](images/c14-i0385.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> is the smallest possible order. The likelihood ratio statistic determines the correct VAR order by testing the significance of coefficient ![images](images/c14-i0386.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mi>A</mi><mi>M</mi></msub></mrow></math> of an upper bound VAR order ![images](images/c14-i0387.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>M</mi></mrow></math>. The null hypothesis ![images](images/c14-i0388.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mn>0</mn><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math> : ![images](images/c14-i0389.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> versus the alternative hypothesis ![images](images/c14-i0390.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math> : ![images](images/c14-i0391.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><mo>&#8800;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> is tested for decreasing values of ![images](images/c14-i0392.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> conditionally on the previous values being true. If ![images](images/c14-i0393.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mn>0</mn><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math> is rejected, the order ![images](images/c14-i0394.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo>&#94;</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></math> is chosen as the optimal order of the VAR process. The likelihood ratio test statistic for testing the ![images](images/c14-i0395.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>\-th null hypothesis solves:

[(14.25)](#c14.xhtml#R_c14-disp-0053)![equation](images/c14-math-0053.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mrow> <mi>L</mi> <mi>R</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>M</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mi>m</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>=</mo> <mi>T</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <mi mathvariant="normal">log</mi> <mi>d</mi> <mi>e</mi> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <msub> <mover accent="true"> <mo>&#931;</mo> <mo>&#732;</mo> </mover> <mi>u</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>m</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mi mathvariant="normal">log</mi> <mi>d</mi> <mi>e</mi> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <msub> <mover accent="true"> <mo>&#931;</mo> <mo>&#732;</mo> </mover> <mi>u</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>m</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

where ![images](images/c14-i0396.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow></math> is the length of the time series and ![images](images/c14-i0397.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mo>&#931;</mo><mo>&#732;</mo></mover><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow></math> is the least square estimator

[(14.26)](#c14.xhtml#R_c14-disp-0054)![equation](images/c14-math-0054.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mover accent="true"> <mo>&#931;</mo> <mo>&#732;</mo> </mover> <mi>u</mi> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mfrac> <mn>1</mn> <mi>T</mi> </mfrac> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>Y</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"> <mi>I</mi> <mi>T</mi> </msub> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <msup> <mi>Z</mi> <mo>&#8242;</mo> </msup> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <msup> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>Z</mi> <msup> <mi>Z</mi> <mo>&#8242;</mo> </msup> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mrow> <mo form="prefix">&#8722;</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </msup> <mi>Z</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mi>Y</mi> <mo>.</mo> </mrow> </math> 

The likelihood ratio test ![images](images/c14-i0398.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mi>R</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math> follows a ![images](images/c14-i0399.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi>&#967;</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math> distribution with ![images](images/c14-i0400.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>K</mi></mrow></math> degrees of freedom.

 

#### *14.3.1.3 Example*

To illustrate the ![images](images/c14-i0401.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>V</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> model, let us model the quarterly and seasonally adjusted West German fixed investment, disposable income and consumption expenditures given in file `e1.csv` available on the book website. The data set comes from Helmut (2005) and is present on the author's website, [http://www.jmulti.de/download/datasets/e1.dat](http://www.jmulti.de/download/datasets/e1.dat).

![](images/c14-gra-0034.png)

We only take the data from 1960 until 1978 and compute the log-return for the three time series. The data set is a ![images](images/c14-i0402.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>&#215;</mo><mn>75</mn></mrow></math> matrix:

![](images/c14-gra-0035.png)

[Figure 14.5](#c14.xhtml#c14-fig-0005) captures the evolution of the Investment (dashed line), disposable income (bold-dashed line), and consumption expenditure (dotted line) between years 1960 and 1978 for West Germany as given by the variable `data`. The log-return version of the data is presented in [Figure 14.6](#c14.xhtml#c14-fig-0006).

![FIGURE 14.5 Investment (dashed line), disposable income (bold-dashed line), and consumption expenditure (dotted line) between years 1960 and 1978 for West Germany as given by the variable data](images/c14f005.png)

[**FIGURE 14.5**](#c14.xhtml#R_c14-fig-0005) Investment (dashed line), disposable income (bold-dashed line), and consumption expenditure (dotted line) between years 1960 and 1978 for West Germany as given by the variable `data`

![FIGURE 14.6 Log-return of the investment, the income, and the consumption between years 1960 and 1978 for West Germany as given by the variable ldata](images/c14f006.png)

[**FIGURE 14.6**](#c14.xhtml#R_c14-fig-0006) Log-return of the investment, the income, and the consumption between years 1960 and 1978 for West Germany as given by the variable `ldata`

We first want to determine the optimal order of the vector autoregressive process for the data set `ldata` containing the three time series: investment (![images](images/c14-i0403.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>S</mi></mrow></math>), disposable income (![images](images/c14-i0404.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>I</mi></mrow></math>) and consumption expenditure (![images](images/c14-i0405.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>). The optimal number of lags is the number ![images](images/c14-i0406.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> such that the parameters ![images](images/c14-i0407.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>&#8800;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c14-i0408.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>:

![equation](images/c14-math-0055.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mfenced open="(" close=")" separators=""><mtable><mtr><mtd columnalign="center"><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub></mtd><mtd columnalign="center"><msub><mi>I</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub></mtd><mtd columnalign="center"><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msub></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center"><msub><mi>S</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mtd><mtd Given an upper bound order ![images](images/c14-i0409.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>M</mi></mrow></math>, the function `.quantQ.ts.varOrder[y;M]` computes the likelihood ratio test statistic ![images](images/c14-i0410.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>L</mi><mi>R</mi></mrow></math> given in [14.25](#c14.xhtml#c14-disp-0053) for ![images](images/c14-i0411.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>;</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math> and the associated ![images](images/c14-i0412.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>\-value. The order ![images](images/c14-i0413.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> is significant at a 0.05 level if ![images](images/c14-i0414.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>l</mi><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#62;</mo><mi>q</mi><msub><mi>&#967;</mi><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>K</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. Based on the ![images](images/c14-i0415.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>\-value, `.quantQ.ts.varOrder[d;4]` shows that the optimal number of lags is 2.

![](images/c14-gra-0036.png)

We then forecast the three time series (![images](images/c14-i0416.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>S</mi></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c14-i0417.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>I</mi></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c14-i0418.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>) with a ![images](images/c14-i0419.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>V</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> model and measure the precision of the estimation by computing an interval of confidence for the forecasted values. The function `.quantQ.ts.tRatios[y;p]` computes the matrix of ![images](images/c14-i0420.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math>\-ratios [14.24](#c14.xhtml#c14-disp-0051) for a matrix of incoming data ![images](images/c14-i0421.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow></math> and lag ![images](images/c14-i0422.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>.

The result of `.quantQ.ts.tRatios[d;2]` is

![](images/c14-gra-0037.png)

The critical values of the ![images](images/c14-i0423.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow></math>\-distribution with ![images](images/c14-i0424.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>&#215;</mo><mn>75</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>&#215;</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>240</mn></mrow></math> degrees of freedom is around 2. The first column corresponds to the t-ratios of the intercept ![images](images/c14-i0425.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#957;</mi></mrow></math>, the 3 next columns equate the t-ratios of ![images](images/c14-i0426.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math>. The last three columns are the t-ratios of ![images](images/c14-i0427.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math>. The estimator of the ![images](images/c14-i0428.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>V</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> model with the log-return times series `ldata`

returns

and

#### *14.3.1.4 Code*

The unbiased estimator of the ![images](images/c14-i0443.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>V</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process given in [14.22](#c14.xhtml#c14-disp-0049) is implemented in the function `.quantQ.ts.varpest`. It uses the vectorisation matrices ![images](images/c14-i0444.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>Y</mi></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c14-i0445.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>Z</mi></mrow></math> introduced in the notation section. First, we implement a vectorisation of a matrix ![images](images/c14-i0446.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></math> denoted as ![images](images/c14-i0447.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>v</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> in the notation section:

![](images/c14-gra-0047.png)

Then, we `compute Zt = (1,y(t),...,y(t-p+1))’`:

![](images/c14-gra-0048.png)

and compute `Z = (zt(y;0;p),...,zt(y;T-p;p))`:

![](images/c14-gra-0049.png)

followed by the computation of `Y = (y(1),...y(T-p))’`:

![](images/c14-gra-0050.png)

We can now implement the estimator of the ![images](images/c14-i0448.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>V</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> model:

![](images/c14-gra-0051.png)

The estimator of the variance-covariance matrix of residual [14.23](#c14.xhtml#c14-disp-0050) is implemented as follows:

![](images/c14-gra-0052.png)

The Likelihood Ratio test statistic used to determine the optimal order of the ![images](images/c14-i0449.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>V</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> process is implemented in `.quantQ.ts.varOrder[y;m]` as a function of the least square or the maximum likelihood estimator of the error [14.26](#c14.xhtml#c14-disp-0054). The function returns a table of three columns. The first column ![images](images/c14-i0450.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> returns the order of the ![images](images/c14-i0451.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>V</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> model, the second column computes ![images](images/c14-i0452.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mi>R</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> as given in [14.25](#c14.xhtml#c14-disp-0053) and the third the ![images](images/c14-i0453.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>\-value of ![images](images/c14-i0454.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mi>R</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.

First, we implement the identity matrix of rank ![images](images/c14-i0455.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow></math>:

Then, we provide a definition of the least square estimator of the error:

### 14.3.2 ![images](images/c14-i0469.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi>V</mi> <mi>A</mi> <mi>R</mi> <mi>X</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>p</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>q</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </math> Process

The VAR model assumes that all stochastic variables of a system (![images](images/c14-i0470.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> in our case) have essentially the same status in that they are all determined within the system. With a VAR model only past values determine its future values. In practice, the generation process may be affected by other observable variables which are determined outside the system of interest. Such variables are called exogenous or unmodelled variables. In contrast, the variables determined within the system are called endogenous. A vector autoregressive process with exogenous variables ![images](images/c14-i0471.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>V</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>R</mi><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> has the following reduced form:

(14.28)![equation](images/c14-math-0059.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mi>y</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mi>A</mi> <mn>1</mn> </msub> <msub> <mi>y</mi> <mrow> <mi>t</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>A</mi> <mi>p</mi> </msub> <msub> <mi>y</mi> <mrow> <mi>t</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mi>p</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>B</mi> <mn>0</mn> </msub> <msub> <mi>x</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>B</mi> <mi>q</mi> </msub> <msub> <mi>x</mi> <mrow> <mi>t</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mi>q</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <msub> <mi>u</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

where ![images](images/c14-i0472.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c14-i0473.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c14-i0474.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c14-i0475.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c14-i0476.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mrow></math> is a ![images](images/c14-i0477.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>K</mi></mrow></math>\-dimensional vector of endogenous variables, ![images](images/c14-i0478.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>M</mi><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mrow></math> is an M-dimensional vector of exogenous variables and ![images](images/c14-i0479.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></math> is white noise.

These types of models are also called transfer function models or distributed lag. In lag operator notation, the reduced form can be written as:

![equation](images/c14-math-0060.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo></mrow></math> 

where ![images](images/c14-i0480.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mi>I</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo>&#8722;</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mi>L</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>&#8722;</mo><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><msup><mi>L</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c14-i0481.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mi>L</mi><mo>+</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><msup><mi>L</mi><mi>q</mi></msup></mrow></math>.

The final form of the system is given by:

![equation](images/c14-math-0061.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>A</mi><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo form="prefix">&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo></mrow></math> 

where ![images](images/c14-i0482.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo form="prefix">&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>. The coefficient matrices ![images](images/c14-i0483.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> of the transfer operator ![images](images/c14-i0484.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mo>&#8721;</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mi>&#8734;</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><msup><mi>L</mi><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow></math> contain the effects that changes in the exogenous variables have on the endogenous variables.

![images](images/c14-i0488.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mi>Y</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> <mo>:</mo> <mo>=</mo> <mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""> <mtable> <mtr> <mtd columnalign="center"> <msub> <mi>y</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> </mtd> </mtr> <mtr> <mtd columnalign="center"> <mo>.</mo> <mo>.</mo> <mo>.</mo> </mtd> </mtr> <mtr> <mtd columnalign="center"> <msub> <mi>y</mi> <mrow> <mi>t</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mi>p</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </msub> </mtd> </mtr> </mtable> </mfenced> </mrow> </math> and ![images](images/c14-i0489.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""><mtable><mtr><mtd columnalign="center"><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center"><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd columnalign="center"><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>&#8722;</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable></mfenced><mo>.</mo></mrow></math>

For a sample of size ![images](images/c14-i0490.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow></math>, the system can be written subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mi>u</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow></math>. Let ![images](images/c14-i0495.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#946;</mi><mo>:</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>v</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>R</mi><mi>&#947;</mi></mrow></math>. The reduced form can be vectorised as ![images](images/c14-i0496.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>Z</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>&#8855;</mo><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mi>I</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>&#946;</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>Z</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>&#8855;</mo><msub subscriptshift="veryverythickmathspace"><mi>I</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>R</mi><mi>&#947;</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>u</mi></mrow></math> with ![images](images/c14-i0497.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>v</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c14-i0498.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>v</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>U</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.

The generalised least squares (GLS) estimator of ![images](images/c14-i0499.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#947;</mi></mrow></math> is:

![equation](images/c14-math-0063.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>&#947;</mi><mo>&#770;</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><msup><mi>R</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><msup><mi>Z</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>&#8855;</mo><msubsup><mo>&#931;</mo><mi>U</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix">&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mo form="prefix">&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mi>R</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>&#8855;</mo><msubsup><mo>&#931;</mo><mi>U</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix">&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>.</mo></mrow></math> 

The variance-covariance matrix of the residual ![images](images/c14-i0500.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mo>&#931;</mo><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow></math> is unknown and can be estimated by OLS. ![equation](images/c14-math-0064.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>&#947;</mi><mo>&#732;</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">\[</mo><msup><mi>R</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><msup><mi>Z</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>&#8855;</mo><mover accent="true"><msubsup><mo>&#931;</mo><mi>u</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix">&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>&#732;</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>R</mi><mo stretchy="false">\]</mo></mrow><mrow><mo form="prefix">&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mi>R</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>&#8855;</mo><mover accent="true"><msubsup><mo>&#931;</mo><mi>u</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix">&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>&#732;</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo></mrow></math> 

with ![images](images/c14-i0503.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mo>&#931;</mo><mo>&#732;</mo></mover><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>&#360;</mi><msup><mi>&#360;</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">/</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></math>.
