so ![images](images/c16-i0207.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">Q</mi></mrow></math> is an unbiased estimator of ![images](images/c16-i0208.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo mathvariant="bold-italic">&#931;</mo></mrow></math>.

Further, closely related to the covariance matrix is the correlation matrix. The correlation matrix, the matrix of Pearson product-moment correlation coefficients between each element in the random vector ![images](images/c16-i0209.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi></mrow></math>, can be written as:

(16.37)![equation](images/c16-math-0027.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="sans-serif">Cor</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\[</mo> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi> <mo stretchy="false">\]</mo> <mo>=</mo> <msup> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <msup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#931;</mi> <mtext>(diag)</mtext> </msup> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mrow> <mo form="prefix">&#8722;</mo> <mfrac> <mn>1</mn> <mn>2</mn> </mfrac> </mrow> </msup> <mo mathvariant="bold-italic">&#931;</mo> <msup> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <msup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#931;</mi> <mtext>(diag)</mtext> </msup> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mrow> <mo form="prefix">&#8722;</mo> <mfrac> <mn>1</mn> <mn>2</mn> </mfrac> </mrow> </msup> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

where ![images](images/c16-i0210.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mo mathvariant="bold-italic">&#931;</mo><mtext>(diag)</mtext></msup></mrow></math> is the matrix of the diagonal elements of ![images](images/c16-i0211.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo mathvariant="bold-italic">&#931;</mo></mrow></math>, i.e. a diagonal matrix of the variances of ![images](images/c16-i0212.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> for each ![images](images/c16-i0213.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow></math>\-th element of ![images](images/c16-i0214.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi></mrow></math>. The sample correlation matrix is obtained accordingly from the sample covariance matrix. By construction, the correlation matrix and the sample correlation matrix are also symmetric and positive semidefinite. Further, all diagonal entries in these matrices are equal to 1. If the variances of all elements of ![images](images/c16-i0215.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi></mrow></math> were equal to 1, then the covariance matrix would be equal to the variance matrix. The correlation matrix is thus a rescaling of the covariance matrix forcing all element variances to be equal.

It is worth establishing a connection between the sample covariance matrix and Gram matrix, ![images](images/c16-i0216.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mfenced open="(" close=")" separators=""><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mfenced><mo>&#8890;</mo></msup><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mrow></math>. In particular, when the data is centred (![images](images/c16-i0217.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mrow></math>), the unbiased sample covariance matrix is given by a scalar multiple of the Gram matrix, namely ![images](images/c16-i0218.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi><mo>&#8890;</mo></msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi></mrow></math>.

 

### 16.4.2 PCA: The First Principal Component

Let us introduce the principal components of the data set provided. We focus on the calculation of the first principal component (PCA), which we will then extend to higher components. For the sake of clarity, let us once again stress that we have ![images](images/c16-i0219.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> features. We shall model our data as a ![images](images/c16-i0220.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>\-dimensional random variable ![images](images/c16-i0221.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msup><mi>&#8477;</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>.

The objective behind the PCA is to look for a vector of weights ![images](images/c16-i0222.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>&#8712;</mo><msup><mi>&#8477;</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> such that the variance of the scalar random variable ![images](images/c16-i0223.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>&#8890;</mo></msup><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is maximised. Thus our objective is to find

(16.38)![equation](images/c16-math-0028.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <munder> <mi>max</mi> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> </munder> <mspace width="0.3em"/> <mi mathvariant="sans-serif">Var</mi> <mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""> <msup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msup> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> </mfenced> <mi>.</mi> </mrow> </math> 

We assume that we are given a data matrix with ![images](images/c16-i0224.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> observations, ![images](images/c16-i0225.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi><mo>&#8712;</mo><msup><mi>&#8477;</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>. Let us centre this data to obtain the centred data matrix ![images](images/c16-i0226.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mrow></math>. We have already argued that the sample covariance matrix:

(16.39)![equation](images/c16-math-0029.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">Q</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mfrac> <mn>1</mn> <mrow> <mi>n</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </mfrac> <msup> <mfenced open="(" close=")" separators=""> <msup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi> <mo>&#8242;</mo> </msup> </mfenced> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msup> <msup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi> <mo>&#8242;</mo> </msup> </mrow> </math> 

is an unbiased estimator of the covariance matrix ![images](images/c16-i0227.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="sans-serif">Var</mi><mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi></mfenced></mrow></math>. Moreover, by the properties of variances,

(16.40)![equation](images/c16-math-0030.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="sans-serif">Var</mi> <mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""> <msup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msup> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> </mfenced> <mo>=</mo> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <mi mathvariant="sans-serif">Var</mi> <mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi> </mfenced> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <mo mathvariant="bold-italic">&#931;</mo> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mi>.</mi> </mrow> </math> 

In practice, however, we don't have access to ![images](images/c16-i0228.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo mathvariant="bold-italic">&#931;</mo></mrow></math>. At best, we can approximate it by some matrix ![images](images/c16-i0229.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi></mrow></math>, say by the unbiased estimator – the sample covariance matrix:

(16.41)![equation](images/c16-math-0031.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">Q</mi> <mo>:</mo> <mo>=</mo> <mfrac> <mn>1</mn> <mrow> <mi>n</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </mfrac> <msup> <mfenced open="(" close=")" separators=""> <msup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi> <mo>&#8242;</mo> </msup> </mfenced> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msup> <msup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi> <mo>&#8242;</mo> </msup> <mi>.</mi> </mrow> </math> 

Thus our maximisation problem becomes:

(16.42)![equation](images/c16-math-0032.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <munder> <mi>max</mi> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> </munder> <mspace width="0.3em"/> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mi>.</mi> </mrow> </math> 

This is not enough; let us add another requirement (in optimisation parlance, another constraint): we want our weights, ![images](images/c16-i0230.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, to be a unit vector:

(16.43)![equation](images/c16-math-0033.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mi>.</mi> </mrow> </math> 

Equivalently, we can add a penalty to our (again, in optimisation parlance) objective function for any deviation from zero of ![images](images/c16-i0231.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8890;</mo></msubsup><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>. The optimisation problem then becomes

(16.44)![equation](images/c16-math-0034.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <munder> <mi>max</mi> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> </munder> <mspace width="0.3em"/> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <msub> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

where the constant ![images](images/c16-i0232.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is a Lagrange multiplier. (This method of including a constraint within the objective function is called the Lagrange multipliers technique.)

Let us now solve this optimisation problem. If ![images](images/c16-i0233.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> maximises our objective function, then

(16.45)![equation](images/c16-math-0035.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mfrac> <mi>&#8706;</mi> <mrow> <mi>&#8706;</mi> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> </mrow> </mfrac> <mfenced open="(" close=")" separators=""> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <msub> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mfenced> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

and, computing the partial derivative on the left-hand side, we get

(16.46)![equation](images/c16-math-0036.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <msub> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mn mathvariant="bold">0</mn> <mi>.</mi> </mrow> </math> 

Rearranging this equation,

(16.47)![equation](images/c16-math-0037.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

we see that ![images](images/c16-i0234.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is an eigenvector of ![images](images/c16-i0235.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c16-i0236.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> the corresponding eigenvalue. And so

(16.48)![equation](images/c16-math-0038.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="sans-serif">Var</mi> <mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""> <msup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msup> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> </mfenced> <mo>&#8776;</mo> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <msub> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mi>.</mi> </mrow> </math> 

From this, since we must maximise ![images](images/c16-i0237.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="sans-serif">Var</mi><mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>&#8890;</mo></msup><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mfenced></mrow></math>, we see that ![images](images/c16-i0238.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is not just any eigenvalue of ![images](images/c16-i0239.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi></mrow></math>, but the largest eigenvalue (and ![images](images/c16-i0240.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> the corresponding eigenvector). We have thus established that ![images](images/c16-i0241.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is the *largest eigenvalue* of ![images](images/c16-i0242.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c16-i0243.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> the corresponding eigenvector.

Note that, if ![images](images/c16-i0244.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi></mrow></math> is a matrix and ![images](images/c16-i0245.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#945;</mi></mrow></math> a non-zero scalar, then

(16.49)![equation](images/c16-math-0039.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">v</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">v</mi> <mo>&#x027FA;</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>&#945;</mi> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">v</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>&#945;</mi> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">v</mi> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

so the eigenvectors of ![images](images/c16-i0246.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#945;</mi><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi></mrow></math> are precisely the eigenvectors of ![images](images/c16-i0247.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi></mrow></math> but the corresponding eigenvalues of ![images](images/c16-i0248.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#945;</mi><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi></mrow></math> are ![images](images/c16-i0249.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>&#945;</mi></mrow></math> times the corresponding eigenvalues of ![images](images/c16-i0250.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">A</mi></mrow></math>. Thus, if we take ![images](images/c16-i0251.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><msup><mfenced open="(" close=")" separators=""><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mfenced><mo>&#8890;</mo></msup><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c16-i0252.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is ![images](images/c16-i0253.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math>, where ![images](images/c16-i0254.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math> is the largest eigenvalue of ![images](images/c16-i0255.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mfenced open="(" close=")" separators=""><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mfenced><mo>&#8890;</mo></msup><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mrow></math>.

Equivalently, ![images](images/c16-i0256.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is ![images](images/c16-i0257.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math> times the square of the largest right singular value of ![images](images/c16-i0258.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c16-i0259.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> the corresponding right singular vector of ![images](images/c16-i0260.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mrow></math>. Recall that, since ![images](images/c16-i0261.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi></mrow></math> is symmetric positive (semi)definite, ![images](images/c16-i0262.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is positive (non-negative). Recall also that, since ![images](images/c16-i0263.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi></mrow></math> is symmetric positive (semi)definite, all its eigenvectors are mutually orthogonal.

 

### 16.4.3 Second Principal Component

We shall now look for a vector of weights ![images](images/c16-i0264.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>&#8712;</mo><msup><mi>&#8477;</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> such that ![images](images/c16-i0265.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is orthogonal to ![images](images/c16-i0266.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> and the variance of the scalar random variable ![images](images/c16-i0267.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>&#8890;</mo></msup><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is maximised. We want this vector to be a unit vector, ![images](images/c16-i0268.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8890;</mo></msubsup><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>. Since it is orthogonal to ![images](images/c16-i0269.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c16-i0270.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8890;</mo></msubsup><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>. We can add this as a constraint to our optimisation problem. We add both constraints to our objective problem using the Lagrange multipliers technique, thus obtaining the objective function:

(16.50)![equation](images/c16-math-0040.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <munder> <mi>max</mi> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> </munder> <mspace width="0.3em"/> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <msub> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <msub> <mi>&#957;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

where![images](images/c16-i0271.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is the Lagrange multiplier corresponding to the unit vector constraint and ![images](images/c16-i0272.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#957;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> the Lagrange multiplier corresponding to the orthogonality constraint.

If ![images](images/c16-i0273.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> maximises our objective function, then

(16.51)![equation](images/c16-math-0041.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mfrac> <mi>&#8706;</mi> <mrow> <mi>&#8706;</mi> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> </mrow> </mfrac> <mfenced open="(" close=")" separators=""> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <msub> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <msub> <mi>&#957;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> </mfenced> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mi>.</mi> </mrow> </math> 

Computing the partial derivative on the left-hand side, we get

(16.52)![equation](images/c16-math-0042.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <msub> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <msub> <mi>&#957;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mn mathvariant="bold">0</mn> <mi>.</mi> </mrow> </math> 

Let us multiply both sides of this equation by ![images](images/c16-i0274.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8890;</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> on the left:

(16.53)![equation](images/c16-math-0043.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <msub> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <msub> <mi>&#957;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mi>.</mi> </mrow> </math> 

Here,

(16.54)![equation](images/c16-math-0044a.png)(16.55)![equation](images/c16-math-0044b.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mtable columnalign="center"> <mtr> <mtd columnalign="center"> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> </mtd> </mtr> <mtr> <mtd columnalign="center"> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>=</mo> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <msub> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>&#183;</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mi>.</mi> </mtd> </mtr> </mtable> </mrow> </math> 

Moreover, since ![images](images/c16-i0275.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c16-i0276.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> are orthogonal and ![images](images/c16-i0277.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is a unit vector, we get

(16.56)![equation](images/c16-math-0045.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mspace width="1em"/> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

and the equation becomes ![images](images/c16-i0278.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#957;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>. Hence

(16.57)![equation](images/c16-math-0046.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <msub> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mn mathvariant="bold">0</mn> <mi>.</mi> </mrow> </math> 

Rearranging this equation,

(16.58)![equation](images/c16-math-0047.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

we see that ![images](images/c16-i0279.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is an eigenvector of ![images](images/c16-i0280.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi></mrow></math> and ![images](images/c16-i0281.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> the corresponding eigenvalue. And so

(16.59)![equation](images/c16-math-0048.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="sans-serif">Var</mi> <mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""> <msup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msup> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> </mfenced> <mo>&#8776;</mo> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <msub> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mi>.</mi> </mrow> </math> 

From this, since we must maximise ![images](images/c16-i0282.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="sans-serif">Var</mi><mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>&#8890;</mo></msup><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mfenced></mrow></math>, we see that ![images](images/c16-i0283.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is not just any eigenvalue of ![images](images/c16-i0284.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi></mrow></math>, but the next largest eigenvalue (after excluding the eigenvalue ![images](images/c16-i0285.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math>) (and ![images](images/c16-i0286.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> the corresponding eigenvector). The eigenvalue ![images](images/c16-i0287.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> is excluded from consideration by the orthogonality constraints on the eigenvectors. Although it may (or may not) happen that ![images](images/c16-i0288.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math>.

We can generalise this process and obtain:

*   The eigenvalue, ![images](images/c16-i0289.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, and the corresponding eigenvector ![images](images/c16-i0290.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, of ![images](images/c16-i0291.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi></mrow></math>, such that ![images](images/c16-i0292.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="sans-serif">Var</mi><mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>&#8890;</mo></msup><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mfenced><mo>&#8776;</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8890;</mo></msubsup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math>;
*   The eigenvalue, ![images](images/c16-i0293.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>&#8804;</mo><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, and the corresponding eigenvector ![images](images/c16-i0294.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, of ![images](images/c16-i0295.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi></mrow></math>, such that ![images](images/c16-i0296.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="sans-serif">Var</mi><mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>&#8890;</mo></msup><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mfenced><mo>&#8776;</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8890;</mo></msubsup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math>;
*   The eigenvalue, ![images](images/c16-i0297.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>&#8804;</mo><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, and the corresponding eigenvector ![images](images/c16-i0298.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, of ![images](images/c16-i0299.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi></mrow></math>, such that ![images](images/c16-i0300.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="sans-serif">Var</mi><mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>&#8890;</mo></msup><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mfenced><mo>&#8776;</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8890;</mo></msubsup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math>;
*   ![images](images/c16-i0301.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi>&#8942;</mi> </mrow> </math>
*   The eigenvalue, ![images](images/c16-i0302.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>&#8804;</mo><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, and the corresponding eigenvector ![images](images/c16-i0303.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, of ![images](images/c16-i0304.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi></mrow></math>, such that ![images](images/c16-i0305.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="sans-serif">Var</mi><mfenced open="\[" close="\]" separators=""><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mo>&#8890;</mo></msup><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mfenced><mo>&#8776;</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>&#8890;</mo></msubsup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>&#955;</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math>.

 

### 16.4.4 Terminology and Explained Variance

It is worth summarising the common terminology used when the PCA is applied. Let ![images](images/c16-i0306.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">W</mi></mrow></math> be the matrix with weights – ![images](images/c16-i0307.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi></mrow></math>’s eigenvectors – as its columns,

(16.60)![equation](images/c16-math-0049.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">W</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mfenced open="(" close=")" separators=""> <mtable> <mtr> <mtd columnalign="center"> <mo stretchy="false">|</mo> </mtd> <mtd columnalign="center"> <mo stretchy="false">|</mo> </mtd> <mtd/> <mtd columnalign="center"> <mo stretchy="false">|</mo> </mtd> </mtr> <mtr> <mtd columnalign="center"> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> </mtd> <mtd columnalign="center"> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> </mtd> <mtd columnalign="center"> <mi>&#8943;</mi> </mtd> <mtd columnalign="center"> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>p</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> </mtd> </mtr> <mtr> <mtd columnalign="center"> <mo stretchy="false">|</mo> </mtd> <mtd columnalign="center"> <mo stretchy="false">|</mo> </mtd> <mtd/> <mtd columnalign="center"> <mo stretchy="false">|</mo> </mtd> </mtr> </mtable> </mfenced> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <msup> <mi>&#8477;</mi> <mrow> <mi>p</mi> <mo>&#215;</mo> <mi>p</mi> </mrow> </msup> <mi>.</mi> </mrow> </math> 

The transformation of the ![images](images/c16-i0308.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>\-dimensional random vector ![images](images/c16-i0309.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi></mrow></math>, centred (corrected for its mean ![images](images/c16-i0310.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#956;</mi></mrow></math>),

(16.61)![equation](images/c16-math-0050.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mi> <mo>=</mo> <msup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">W</mi> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msup> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi> <mo>&#8722;</mo> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#956;</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <msup> <mi>&#8477;</mi> <mrow> <mi>p</mi> <mo>&#215;</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </msup> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

the ![images](images/c16-i0311.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>\-dimensional random vector ![images](images/c16-i0312.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mi></mrow></math>, is called the vector of ![images](images/c16-i0313.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi></mrow></math>’s principal components or principal component (PC) scores. The ![images](images/c16-i0314.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow></math>\-th element of ![images](images/c16-i0315.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">y</mi></mrow></math> is then the ![images](images/c16-i0316.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow></math>\-th principal component or the ![images](images/c16-i0317.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow></math>\-th PC score of ![images](images/c16-i0318.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi></mrow></math>.

For the centred data matrix ![images](images/c16-i0319.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi><mo mathvariant="bold-italic">&#8242;</mo></msup><mo>&#8712;</mo><msup><mi>&#8477;</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>, the principal components or principal component (PC) scores are given by the matrix

(16.62)![equation](images/c16-math-0051.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">Z</mi> <mo>:</mo> <mo>=</mo> <msup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi> <mo mathvariant="bold-italic">&#8242;</mo> </msup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">W</mi> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <msup> <mi>&#8477;</mi> <mrow> <mi>n</mi> <mo>&#215;</mo> <mi>p</mi> </mrow> </msup> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

so that the ![images](images/c16-i0320.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>\-th entry of ![images](images/c16-i0321.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">Z</mi></mrow></math>,

(16.63)![equation](images/c16-math-0052.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msub> <mi>Z</mi> <mrow> <mi>i</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>j</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi> <mrow> <mi>i</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mo>:</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8242;</mo> </msubsup> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>j</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

with ![images](images/c16-i0322.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c16-i0323.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>, where ![images](images/c16-i0324.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">x</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mo>:</mo></mrow><mo>&#8242;</mo></msubsup></mrow></math> is the ![images](images/c16-i0325.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow></math>\-th row of ![images](images/c16-i0326.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mrow></math>, is the ![images](images/c16-i0327.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>j</mi></mrow></math>\-th principal component (![images](images/c16-i0328.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>j</mi></mrow></math>\-th PC score) of the ![images](images/c16-i0329.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow></math>\-th observation (the ![images](images/c16-i0330.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow></math>\-th row of ![images](images/c16-i0331.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi><mo>&#8242;</mo></msup></mrow></math>). The ![images](images/c16-i0332.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>j</mi></mrow></math>\-th column of ![images](images/c16-i0333.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">Z</mi></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c16-i0334.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>&#8804;</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c16-i0335.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">z</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math>, is sometimes referred to as the ![images](images/c16-i0336.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>j</mi></mrow></math>\-th principal component of the data. Thus the ![images](images/c16-i0337.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>j</mi></mrow></math>\-th weight vector, ![images](images/c16-i0338.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>&#8712;</mo><msup><mi>&#8477;</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>&#215;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>, maps the data to the ![images](images/c16-i0339.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi>j</mi></mrow></math>\-th principal component (PC score). Since![images](images/c16-i0340.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">W</mi></mrow></math> is an orthogonal matrix, its inverse is given by its transpose, ![images](images/c16-i0341.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">W</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix">&#8722;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">W</mi><mo>&#8890;</mo></msup></mrow></math>, and so the inverse transform is obtained from

(16.64)![equation](images/c16-math-0053.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <msup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi> <mo>&#8242;</mo> </msup> <mo>=</mo> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">Z</mi> <msup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">W</mi> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msup> <mo>=</mo> <msup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi> <mo>&#8242;</mo> </msup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">W</mi> <msup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">W</mi> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msup> <mo>=</mo> <msup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">X</mi> <mo>&#8242;</mo> </msup> <mi>.</mi> </mrow> </math> 

Sometimes the weights – the columns of ![images](images/c16-i0342.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">W</mi></mrow></math>, ![images](images/c16-i0343.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>&#8230;</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></math> – are referred to as loadings. However, it is possible to find also the following as loadings – the columns of ![images](images/c16-i0344.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">W</mi></mrow></math> scaled up by the square roots of the corresponding eigenvalues:

(16.65)![equation](images/c16-math-0054.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">L</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mfenced open="(" close=")" separators=""> <mtable> <mtr> <mtd columnalign="center"> <mo stretchy="false">|</mo> </mtd> <mtd columnalign="center"> <mo stretchy="false">|</mo> </mtd> <mtd/> <mtd columnalign="center"> <mo stretchy="false">|</mo> </mtd> </mtr> <mtr> <mtd columnalign="center"> <msqrt> <msub> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> </msqrt> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> </mtd> <mtd columnalign="center"> <msqrt> <msub> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> </msqrt> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> </mtd> <mtd columnalign="center"> <mi>&#8943;</mi> </mtd> <mtd columnalign="center"> <msqrt> <msub> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>p</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> </msqrt> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>p</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> </mtd> </mtr> <mtr> <mtd columnalign="center"> <mo stretchy="false">|</mo> </mtd> <mtd columnalign="center"> <mo stretchy="false">|</mo> </mtd> <mtd/> <mtd columnalign="center"> <mo stretchy="false">|</mo> </mtd> </mtr> </mtable> </mfenced> <mo>&#8712;</mo> <msup> <mi>&#8477;</mi> <mrow> <mi>p</mi> <mo>&#215;</mo> <mi>p</mi> </mrow> </msup> <mi>.</mi> </mrow> </math> 

Because of this ambiguity, we shall avoid this term altogether. Note that there is quite a lot of ambiguity and confusion in the terminology associated with the PCA, especially across different fields.



by orthogonality, the distinct principal components are uncorrelated.

It also common to connect the PCA with explanation of variance. The question arises: In what sense do the principal components “explain the variance”? It is a fact from linear algebra that, since ![images](images/c16-i0346.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi></mrow></math> is symmetric positive, it is diagonalisable as

(16.72)![equation](images/c16-math-0056.png)<math display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll"> <mrow> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">W</mi> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">&#923;</mi> <msup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">W</mi> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msup> <mo>=</mo> <munderover> <mo>&#8721;</mo> <mrow> <mi>i</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> <mi>p</mi> </munderover> <msub> <mi>&#955;</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>i</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <msub> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>i</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> </msub> <msubsup> <mi mathvariant="bold-italic">w</mi> <mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>i</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>&#8890;</mo> </msubsup> <mo>,</mo> </mrow> </math> 

where ![images](images/c16-i0347.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">W</mi></mrow></math> is a matrix with ![images](images/c16-i0348.png)<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline" overflow="scroll"><mrow><mi mathvariant="bold-italic">C</mi></mrow></math>’s eigenvectors as its columns:
